user.title: Add a surf spot
user.description: Enter your Stormglass API key and pick the break you want to forecast. You will set which way the beach faces on the next screen.

shore.title: Which way does the beach face?

menu_options.shore_map: Drag a pin into the water (easiest)

shore_map.title: Drag the pin into the water
shore_map.description:
The map is centred on your break, with the pin sitting on it.

**Drag the pin straight out into the open water** in front of the break — any distance beyond about 50 m — and the direction the beach faces is worked out from where it lands. You will see the result as a compass bearing on the next screen before anything is saved.

The map only shows one marker, so it will not leave a pin behind on the break itself.

shore_manual.title: Confirm the shore direction
shore_manual.description:
{estimate}

The bearing is the way the beach looks out to sea: 180 is south-facing, 270 is west-facing.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Stormglass. Check your connection and try again.
error.sea_point_too_close: The pin is still on the break. Drag it out into the water, at least 50 m away, so there is a direction to measure.

abort.already_configured: That spot is already set up.

init.title: Surf spot options
init.description: The free Stormglass plan allows 10 requests per day. Each refresh costs one request for the forecast, plus one each for tide and astronomy when those need renewing. A 6 hour interval lands at roughly 6 requests per day.

data.ideal_min_height: Smallest wave height you consider good
data.ideal_max_height: Largest wave height you consider good
data.good_surf_threshold: Rating that counts as good surf
data.enable_astronomy: Fetch sunrise, sunset and moon data

error.ideal_range_invalid: The smallest good wave height must be below the largest.

shore_direction_suspect.title: Check the shore direction for {name}
shore_direction_suspect.description:
{name} is configured as facing {configured} degrees, but the forecast has swell arriving from {wave_from} degrees, which is {offset} degrees away from straight onshore. Waves cannot reach a break from inland, so the shore direction is probably wrong and the offshore/onshore wind rating will be inverted.

Based on where the swell is coming from, something near {suggested} degrees is more likely. You can change it in the integration's options.
